name: Creator Motion Graphics
look: The high-energy business-creator edit: huge condensed caps slamming in word by word, a yellow serif accent on the one word that matters, highlighter swipes, hand-drawn circles and arrows, tilted browser and phone mockups, rolling green counters, film grain and light leaks on near-black.
how: Every idea gets its own beat: words land on the beat with punch zooms and shake, the wrong idea gets a red strike and a stamp, proof appears as code-drawn mockups, the key number rolls up and locks with a boom, and whip pans, RGB glitches and flash cuts carry you between scenes.
demo: How to land your first client
replace: TL, CUTS, PUNCH, SHAKE, FLASH, LEAK, PUSH, the value curves, the scene functions, SCENES, the chrome() label text and scoreSound()
keep: slam, row, swipe, slamMarked, strike, scribble, handArrow, drawYaw, bubble, background, finishing and the compositor
sizes: keep statement text at 80 px or more, any label the story depends on at 28 px or more, and key numbers at 120 px or more
voLine: Every on-screen word slams in at the start of its spoken word, within 0.03 s. Show 2 to 6 key words per sentence, not a full transcript.
full: - Full mix (no voiceover): keep the music, have at most about 3 sounds at once, and leave a moment of near-silence before the biggest hit.
voMix: - Voiceover mix: the player calls SFX.live with { voiceover: true } once narration is loaded, which keeps the music low and plays anything marked soft at about 55%. Mark small sounds (pops, ticks, markers, keys) soft: true. Keep booms for the 2 or 3 biggest moments, never put a riser over a spoken sentence, and keep the drone out from under speech.
sheet: Surface: a near-black editing-room background with slow warm and cool glows, a faint drifting grid, a vignette and film grain stepped at 24 fps. Run background() and finishing() on every frame at the reference’s strength.

Type: Anton in caps for statements, set big (80 to 220 px). Instrument Serif italic in yellow for the one soft or emotional phrase. Inter for labels and small supporting lines. At most one yellow word per line; green only for money and growth numbers; red only for the wrong idea.

Numbers: a rolling counter in green with a glow. When it locks: a boom, a white flash, a light leak and spark streaks.

Proof shots: stylized mockups drawn in code (browser pages, phone chats, dashboards, cards) with invented, generic names. No real logos, brand names or real people, and nothing that would pass as a real receipt or a real message. Label figures as examples when they are illustrative.

Pace: the hook lands in under 2 seconds, something new happens every 0.5 to 1.5 seconds, and the takeaway holds about 1.5 seconds at the end.

name: Chalk Talk
look: A teacher at a long green slate: grainy chalk strokes that skip over the board’s tooth, colored chalk for emphasis, dust falling from the stick as it writes, faint ghosts of old lessons, a wooden frame and a dusty chalk tray.
how: One continuous lesson along the board: a visible chalk stick writes every word and draws every line, the camera tracks to the next stretch of slate, numbers are re-chalked as they count, pink chalk rings the key moments, and a felt eraser wipes a section clean for the takeaway.
replace: TL, CAM, the counter curve (cntStep, cntVal, cntText), ITEMS, drawCounter(), WIPE and its timing, and scoreSound()
keep: board(), tooth(), noise2, chalkLine, chalkText, layoutText, resample, quad, ellipse, wipeMask, the frame and tray, the chalk stick, the eraser, dust() and the compositor
sizes: keep headings at 90 px or more, chalked writing at 56 px or more, labels at 36 px or more, and key numbers at 72 px or more
voLine: Each line of chalk starts being written as its first word is spoken and finishes by the end of that phrase; a short label can land on a single word. Write the key phrase on the board, not the whole transcript.
full: - Full mix (no voiceover): room tone, chalk and eraser sounds, and soft plucks on the big moments. No music.
voMix: - Voiceover mix: the player calls SFX.live with { voiceover: true } once narration is loaded. Mark chalk scratches and taps soft: true so they sit under the voice, keep the room tone very low, and keep plucks for the 2 or 3 biggest moments only.
sheet: Surface: one long slate (BW wide, 720 tall) baked once with mottled green, faint chalk ghosts of old lessons and old eraser smears. The tooth pattern is punched out of the chalk layer every frame so strokes break like real chalk. Keep the wooden frame, the tray with chalk pieces, the classroom light falloff and the fine grain.

Writing: everything appears by being chalked on in order. Letters arrive one at a time with a little jitter; lines are drawn along their path with small skips. The chalk stick follows the tip whenever something is being written, and dust falls from it.

Type: Cabin Sketch for titles and the big takeaway, Kalam for equations, labels and notes. White chalk for content, yellow for the main idea and curves, pink for emphasis and key numbers, blue for side notes. Exponents and small marks use the dy offset on text parts.
Camera: one board, one continuous shot. The camera tracks along the slate to a fresh stretch for each new idea (CAM keys) and leans in gently on the key moment. No cuts.
Emphasis: pink rings around the key number or point, yellow underlines and brackets, chalk arrows that lead the eye along the board.
Numbers: re-chalked as they count (a fresh scrawl about 10 times a second), then ringed when they land.
Scene change: the felt eraser wipes a section back and forth, leaving a faint haze, and the next idea is written in the cleared space.
Diagrams: draw real charts to scale for the topic, with axes, labels and curves computed from the actual function.
Pace: something is always being written. Allow 0.4 to 1.2 seconds per line and hold the takeaway about 1.5 seconds.
sound: Bed: quiet room tone only, no music. A double knock on the board can open the lesson.

Chalk: every word gets its own scratch (grainy band-passed noise bursts with a tap where the stick lands), timed by character position across its write window. Lines get one long scratch; rings and underlines a little louder. Use the score helpers tap, scratch, write and pluck, built on k.hiss and k.voice.
Counter: a short scratch each time the shown number changes. Eraser: a felt swish for each pass, panned with the eraser.
Big moments: soft plucked notes, two for a landed number and a rising arpeggio for the takeaway. Keep it gentle; this is a lesson, not a trailer.

Look: A polished screen-recording tutorial built entirely in code: an app window on a soft gradient desktop, a real-feeling cursor with click ripples, a camera that zooms into what matters, yellow-edged spotlights, numbered step callouts and a calm pad underneath.
How it explains: It shows the clicks, not just the idea: a title card, then the cursor moves through the real flow while the camera follows it in and out, modals and menus open, fields get typed, toggles flip, and a dark step pill at the bottom left counts you through. It ends on the result actually happening and a short lower third.

I want an animated video in the "Software Walkthrough" style (Screen and UI) from the Motion Graphics Style Library. Below is a complete, working reference animation in this style: its core helpers (CM), a synthesized sound kit (SFX), the style's scenes, its sound score and the player page. Treat that file as the ground truth for how this style looks, moves and sounds, and rebuild it around my content.

MY CONTENT
[No topic yet. Ask me for my topic or script before building anything.]

VOICEOVER TIMING
[No timing pasted yet. Before building, ask me for a word-level SRT or word timestamps of my voiceover. If I only have the audio file, offer to transcribe it into word timings.]

How to use the timing:
- Turn it into a list of words with start and end times in seconds. If the timing is per line only, spread each line's words across its span in proportion to their length.
- Set the duration to the last word's end plus about 1.2 seconds.
- Build the timeline (TL) from these times. Each click lands on the spoken word that names it, the camera starts moving about 0.3 s before the thing it shows is mentioned, and each step pill appears as its step is introduced.
- Cut between scenes only at idea boundaries (a new step, a new claim, a reveal), never mid-word, and finish each cut just before the next idea's first spoken word.
- Put the emphasis moves on stressed words. A counter lands at the exact moment its number is spoken.
- Keep the player's "Load voiceover" button working so I can drop in my audio and hear it in sync.

STORYBOARD FIRST
Before building, show me a storyboard and wait for my OK:
- One HTML page (an artifact if you can) with a grid of 6 to 10 panels, one per beat. Draw each panel on a canvas with the reference's own helpers, scene drawing and finishing pass, so the stills already look like the finished piece. No animation or sound yet.
- Under each panel: the beat number, its start and end time, the exact on-screen words, the camera move or emphasis, how it gets there from the previous beat (the same scene continuing, or a cut and which kind), and its key sounds.
- Below the grid, list any facts or numbers you had to assume.
When I approve it (or after my changes), build the full animation and reuse the storyboard's drawing code.

WHAT TO BUILD
One self-contained HTML file (an artifact if you can), built on the reference file below:
- Keep the page, the player (play/pause, scrub, time, sound toggle, loop, Load voiceover) and the CM and SFX blocks unchanged.
- Replace the demo's story: TL, CAM, CURSOR, STEP_NAMES, the app pieces (sidebar, header, homePage, emptyState, modal, editor), the spotlight calls in explainer(), titleCard(), notification(), outroCard() and scoreSound(). Keep and reuse the style's helpers (the ui-kit helpers (rr, track, rise, riseLine, typed, softCard, cursorArrow, checkMark, padBed), wallpaper(), appWindow() as the frame, spotlight(), cursor(), stepCallout() and the camera transform in explainer()).
- Aim for 15 to 40 seconds unless my content needs more, and set the duration in TL.D.
- Keep window.seek(t), window.DURATION, window.scoreSound and window.SFX exposed, so the video can be rendered frame by frame.
- Load the style's fonts before the first draw, as the reference does: DM Sans (400 to 700), DM Mono (400 and 500).

THE STYLE
- Surface: a desktop with a soft indigo to teal gradient wallpaper and two slow light blooms. On it, one app window (rounded, deep shadow) with a title bar, a sidebar and a main area. - Type: DM Sans for all UI and titles (700 for headings and selected items, 400 to 500 for body), DM Mono in caps for tiny labels (WHEN, THEN, LIVE). No chimes, bells, pings, sparkles or risers, and no music beat. Never more than 2 sounds at once.

# Motion graphics style #102: Metamorphosis Specimen

- **ID:** `metamorphosis-specimen`

- **Canvas:** `1280x720`

- **Footage Overlay:** No

Scientific biological documentary: deep navy cyan blueprint grid alternating with warm colored-pencil specimen illustrations, circular microscope loupe overlays with measurement calipers, and synthesized marimba/bell score.

## How It Explains
Microscopic life-cycle progression: cross-sectional blueprint views cut to organic hand-drawn details, magnifying reticles zoom into cellular structures, stage indicators step forward, and delicate lines animate organic growth.

## Demo
The metamorphosis of the monarch butterfly

---

Treat that file as the ground truth for how this style looks, moves and sounds, and rebuild it around my content.

MY CONTENT
[No topic yet. Ask me for my topic or script before building anything.]

BUILD DIRECTLY
Skip the storyboard and build the full animation now. Afterwards, list any facts or numbers you assumed.

WHAT TO BUILD
One self-contained HTML file (an artifact if you can), built on the reference file:
- Keep the page player (play/pause, scrub, time, sound toggle, loop) and core motion helpers unchanged.
- Replace the demo story: TL, CUTS, specimen illustration curves, microscopy zoom coordinates, anatomical labels, and musical scale cues. Keep and reuse the style's core mechanics: dual navy blueprint / colored-pencil compositor, circular magnifying loupe with measurement ticks, organic path evolution, marimba synthesizer.
- Aim for 15 to 45 seconds unless my content needs more, and set the duration in window.DURATION.
- Keep window.seek(t), window.DURATION, and deterministic rendering exposed so the video renders frame by frame via headless Chrome and FFmpeg.
- Load the style's fonts before first draw: Cinzel, Caveat, JetBrains Mono.

- Surface: alternating between deep navy cyan blueprint grid (#0b192c, #1e3e62) with fine white engineering lines and warm botanical drawing paper (#f8f5ee).

RULES THAT KEEP IT IN STYLE
- Change the story, words and props; do not change the medium. Draw every subject accurately for my topic.
- Every frame is a pure function of time t. Use seeded PRNG and deterministic sine/spring curves for all randomness, never unseeded Math.random.
- It will be watched on phones and monitors: keep scientific title at 80 px or more, anatomical labels at 30 px or more, scale markings at 22 px or more. Fill the frame.
- Keep each frame render fast, well under 30 ms.
